summary: Ahead of Chelsea's home derby against Arsenal, Mauricio Pochettino defended captain Reece James, who lost his temper with an official after the 1-0 home defeat to Aston Villa on 24 September and has been out with hamstring problems. Pochettino called it a mistake, praised James's passion and 'Chelsea DNA', and drew parallels with his own emotional nature and his long friendship with Arsenal's Mikel Arteta. He also played down the idea that the Arsenal game is a statement match, stressing Chelsea's injury issues and their position of 11th in the table.
one_line: Pochettino backs injured Chelsea captain Reece James after his tunnel outburst, citing his passion and 'Chelsea DNA', ahead of the Arsenal derby.
key_facts: Reece James, named Chelsea captain by Mauricio Pochettino, has not played since the opening weekend draw with Liverpool at Stamford Bridge, when he injured a hamstring.
Chelsea lost 1-0 at home to Aston Villa on 24 September, their second consecutive home Premier League defeat after Nottingham Forest, and were booed off; Malo Gusto was controversially sent off.
James lost his cool with an official in the tunnel after the Villa game, and the Football Association announced a charge for abusive conduct three days later.
James was still injured for the 2 October trip to Fulham, so a likely one-match ban did not apply until the 7 October game at Burnley.
The 23-year-old James was not called up by England for the recent internationals, and there are reports of a hamstring setback and possible surgery.
Pochettino said James's hamstring is 'much better' but not 100%, and James will probably be a substitute against Arsenal; Gusto is available again after suspension.
Pochettino described James's outburst as a mistake: 'we all make them and he was really sorry about it', adding 'That's it. Finish.'
Pochettino chose James as captain for 'his personality, his leadership, the respect he has from the club and his teammates … he has Chelsea DNA', as an appointment 'for the present and the future'.
Pochettino was booked for dissent during the Burnley game and sees similarities between himself and James.
Pochettino and Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta joined Paris Saint-Germain in early 2001, when Pochettino was 28 and Arteta 18; Pochettino calls Arteta 'family'.
Chelsea won at Fulham and Burnley and beat Brighton in the Carabao Cup on the day James was charged.
After Arsenal, Chelsea face Brentford, Tottenham, Manchester City, Newcastle, Brighton and Manchester United; they sit 11th and will be without seven players through injury against Arsenal.
Pochettino rejected the idea that the Arsenal game would be a statement win, saying Chelsea cannot say 'Be careful, Chelsea is coming' under current circumstances.
